R0286.title: Liquidity Deception Risk
R0286.definition: Attackers manufacture, hide, shift, or disguise liquidity so counterparties or models misjudge market depth, execution capacity, and price impact.
R0286.description:
Liquidity deception occurs in order books, cross-venue trading, OTC, dark pools, virtual-asset pools, and market-making systems. Attackers may create ghost liquidity, liquidity illusion, hidden liquidity, liquidity vacuum, cross-venue liquidity shifts, or false-break liquidity inducement so traders misjudge executable size and price resilience.

This differs from ordinary low liquidity. The focus is intentional use of visible depth, hidden orders, venue fragmentation, and trade-display rules to create false signals. Impacts include wider slippage for large orders, stop-loss triggering, false breakout judgments, and market-maker exposure.
R0286.influence: It causes counterparties to misjudge depth and executable size, exposing large orders to slippage, false breakouts, stop-loss triggers, or sudden liquidity disappearance.

observables: Visible depth disappears as execution approaches
Cross-venue depth and prices diverge sharply for the same instrument
Liquidity withdraws after a breakout signal and price reverses quickly
Split large orders experience price impact far above baseline
